claim.en: Good children never say no to elders.
claim.hg: Achhe bacche badon ko kabhi 'no' nahi bolte.

fact.en: Respecting elders is good. But respect does not mean saying yes to everything. If something feels unsafe, hurts you or has to be kept secret, you can say no, even to an elder. Then tell a grown-up you trust. Saying no does not make you a bad child. And if you could not say no, it is still not your fault.
fact.hg: Badon ki respect karna achhi baat hai. Par respect ka matlab har cheez pe 'yes' bolna nahi hai. Agar koi cheez unsafe lage, usse tumhe hurt ho ya use secret rakhne ko bola jaye, toh tum 'no' bol sakte ho, kisi bade ko bhi. Phir kisi bharose wale bade ko batao. 'No' bolne se tum bure bacche nahi ban jaate. Aur agar tum 'no' nahi bol paaye, tab bhi yeh tumhari galti nahi hai.

why.en: Children are taught to obey elders because elders usually care for them and know more. So people forget to add that some things are okay to refuse.
why.hg: Bacchon ko badon ki baat maanna sikhaya jata hai kyunki bade usually unka khayal rakhte hain aur zyada jaante hain. Isliye log yeh add karna bhool jaate hain ki kuch cheezon ko mana karna theek hai.

claim.en: Telling a teacher or parent about a problem is 'chugli' (tattling).
claim.hg: Teacher ya parents ko kisi problem ke baare mein batana chugli hai.

fact.en: Tattling is telling just to get someone into trouble over a small thing. Telling is different. When someone is being hurt, scared, bullied or touched in a wrong way, telling a grown-up is how you get help. That is brave, not chugli.
fact.hg: Chugli woh hai jab kisi chhoti-si baat pe bas kisi ko daant padwane ke liye bataya jaye. Batana alag cheez hai. Jab kisi ko hurt kiya ja raha ho, daraya ja raha ho, bully kiya ja raha ho ya galat tareeke se touch kiya ja raha ho, toh kisi bade ko batane se hi help milti hai. Yeh bahaduri hai, chugli nahi.

why.en: Children do not want friends to call them a 'complaint box'. Sometimes grown-ups also say 'don't complain' when they are busy.
why.hg: Bacche nahi chahte ki dost unhe 'complaint box' bolein. Kabhi-kabhi bade bhi busy hone pe bol dete hain 'complain mat karo'.

claim.en: Saying sorry first means you lost the fight.
claim.hg: Pehle sorry bolne ka matlab hai tum fight haar gaye.

fact.en: An apology is not a scorecard. Saying sorry for your part shows that the friendship matters more to you than winning. It usually lowers the other person's guard and makes them more willing to admit their part. You can apologise for what you did and still explain what hurt you. People who can do both are the ones others trust.
fact.hg: Apology koi scorecard nahi hai. Apne part ke liye sorry bolna dikhata hai ki tumhare liye jeetne se zyada dosti matter karti hai. Isse usually saamne wale ka guard neeche aata hai aur woh bhi apni galti maanne ko zyada ready hota hai. Tum apne kiye ke liye sorry bolkar bhi bata sakte ho ki tumhe kis baat se hurt hua. Jo log ye dono kar paate hain, unhi pe doosre trust karte hain.

why.en: Films, games and even family arguments often treat backing down as weakness, so many people learn to wait for the other side to bend first.
why.hg: Films, games aur yahan tak ki ghar ki arguments bhi aksar peeche hatne ko weakness maanti hain, isliye bahut log yahi seekhte hain ki pehle saamne wala jhuke.

claim.en: If a health video has millions of views, it must be correct.
claim.hg: Agar kisi health video pe millions views hain, toh woh sahi hi hoga.

fact.en: Views measure attention, not accuracy. Platforms promote content that people watch and share, and dramatic or frightening claims get shared more than careful ones. Many viral health videos are made by people with no medical training or with something to sell. Judge a claim by who made it, what evidence it gives and whether reliable health sources agree, never by the view count.
fact.hg: Views attention measure karte hain, accuracy nahi. Platforms usi content ko promote karte hain jo log dekhte aur share karte hain, aur dramatic ya darane wale claims careful claims se zyada share hote hain. Bahut saare viral health videos aise log banate hain jinke paas koi medical training nahi hoti ya jinhe kuch bechna hota hai. Kisi claim ko isse judge karo ki use kisne banaya, woh kya evidence deta hai aur kya reliable health sources usse agree karte hain, view count se kabhi nahi.

why.en: We naturally assume that if so many people watched and liked something, someone must have checked it. Popularity feels like proof, especially when friends forward it too.
why.hg: Hum naturally maan lete hain ki jab itne logon ne koi cheez dekhi aur like ki hai, toh kisi ne use check kiya hi hoga. Popularity proof jaisi lagti hai, khaaskar jab dost bhi use forward karein.

claim.en: If you keep asking and they finally say yes, that counts as a real yes.
claim.hg: Agar tum poochte raho aur finally woh 'yes' bol dein, toh woh asli 'yes' count hogi.

fact.en: A yes given to end nagging, guilt or pressure is giving in, not agreeing. Real agreement is free and willing, and the person could have said no without being punished. Asking once is fine; asking again and again after a no is pressure. If someone says no, the respectful and safe response is to stop asking.
fact.hg: Zid, guilt ya pressure se peecha chhudane ke liye di gayi 'yes' haar maan lena hai, agree karna nahi. Asli agreement free aur willing hota hai, aur usme insaan bina kisi punishment ke 'no' bhi bol sakta tha. Ek baar poochna theek hai; 'no' ke baad baar-baar poochna pressure hai. Agar koi 'no' bole, toh respectful aur safe response yahi hai ki poochna band kar do.

why.en: Films and songs often show a hero who refuses to give up and is rewarded in the end, so persistence gets mistaken for romance or confidence.
why.hg: Films aur songs mein aksar aisa hero dikhaya jata hai jo give up nahi karta aur end mein use reward milta hai, isliye peeche pade rehne ko romance ya confidence samajh liya jata hai.

claim.en: You do not owe anyone an explanation for saying no to something that crosses your boundary.
claim.hg: Jo cheez tumhari boundary cross karti hai, use 'no' bolne ke liye tumhe kisi ko explanation dene ki zaroorat nahi.

fact.en: True. 'No' is a complete answer. You may give a reason if you want to, and with people you trust it can help them understand. But your boundary is valid without one, and nobody is entitled to debate it. Long explanations often invite argument, so a short, calm 'No, I'm not comfortable with that' is usually the most effective reply.
fact.hg: Sahi. 'No' apne aap mein complete answer hai. Tum chaho toh reason de sakte ho, aur jinpe tumhe trust hai unhe isse samajhne mein help mil sakti hai. Par tumhari boundary bina reason ke bhi valid hai, aur kisi ko uspe debate karne ka haq nahi. Lambi explanations aksar argument ko invite karti hain, isliye short, calm 'Nahi, main isme comfortable nahi hoon' usually sabse effective reply hota hai.

why.en: Many of us are raised to justify every refusal so that nobody feels bad. It can come as a surprise that a polite, firm no without reasons is acceptable.
why.hg: Hum mein se bahuton ko yahi sikhaya gaya hai ki har refusal ko justify karo taaki kisi ko bura na lage. Isliye yeh jaankar surprise ho sakta hai ki bina reason ke polite, firm 'no' bhi acceptable hai.

claim.en: Whatever you tell a doctor always stays completely secret.
claim.hg: Doctor ko tum jo bhi batao, woh hamesha completely secret rehta hai.

fact.en: Partly true. Confidentiality is a basic duty of doctors, and they should not share your information casually. But it has limits. If you are under 18, the law requires them to report sexual abuse or sexual activity involving a minor, and a guardian is usually involved in consent. Doctors may also act if there is serious danger to life. You can always ask how your information will be used.
fact.hg: Partly sahi. Confidentiality doctors ki basic duty hai, aur unhe tumhari information casually share nahi karni chahiye. Par iski limits hain. Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh law ke hisaab se unhe kisi minor ke saath sexual abuse ya sexual activity report karni hoti hai, aur consent mein usually guardian involved hote hain. Life ko serious danger ho toh bhi doctors action le sakte hain. Tum hamesha pooch sakte ho ki tumhari information kaise use hogi.

why.en: People hear that doctors must keep secrets, which is broadly right, and assume there are no exceptions. The limits are rarely explained to patients, especially young ones.
why.hg: Log sunte hain ki doctors ko baatein secret rakhni hoti hain, jo broadly sahi hai, aur maan lete hain ki iska koi exception nahi. Ye limits patients ko, khaaskar young logon ko, kam hi explain ki jaati hain.
